note: V92Jd's constructor is V90Jd's plus a fixed-point conversion through the coprocessor, and the two differ in three small ways that a reconstruction assembled from the V.90 one would get wrong: the second rate group is ELEVEN bits and not twelve, `bits[47]` is stored as a constant 0 rather than copied from a parameter, and the phase message's three trailing bytes are set to 1, 0, 0.  Every one of those is a mutation below.  The scale mutations exist because the conversion is the only arithmetic in the file: 65536 is 16 bits of fraction, and a reconstruction that used 32768 agrees with the object on exactly the values that happen to be even.

label: the fixed-point scale is one bit out
the phase is rounded rather than truncated
the phase is read from the neighbouring parameter
the phase bits start one place up the word
the phase loop is one bit short
the second rate group runs to V90Jd's twelve bits
the first rate group is one bit short
find:
for (i = 0; i <= 15; i++)
		bits[V90JD_GROUP1 + 1 + i] = (unsigned char)((mask >> i) & 1);
replace:
for (i = 0; i <= 14; i++)
		bits[V90JD_GROUP1 + 1 + i] = (unsigned char)((mask >> i) & 1);

label: the rate mask is read from the V.90 parameter
the phase message's leading constant is cleared, not set
the data message's constant is set, not cleared
the phase message's two trailing bytes are left as they were
the two lookahead bits are transposed
the phase unpacker's word is left as it was
the destructor is not empty
why: GCC's `-flifetime-dse` is on at -O2 and deletes stores to `*this` in a destructor, so the mutated body and the empty one compile to the identical bare `ret`.  See v90jd.json's entry of the same name.
